To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have for the first time developed an analytical model that accounts for the three major workload components of airspace capacity and that we have for all 20 continental United States centers estimated the capacity parameters for the workload equation and validated the analytical model with peak traffic counts from the National Airspace System.
the capacity of a sector is proportional to the number of aircraft in the sector raised to the 1/3rd power.

the capacity model is validated with peak count data, that the model is a function of the number of sectors in a center and the number of sectors with which each sector communicates, that the inherent capacity of a center is a function of its sector count, that the achieved capacity of a center depends on the number of sectors that reach capacity, and that the achieved capacity is less than the inherent capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
validating a new capacity equation with data from the US national airspace system.
the validation of a capacity model with peak counts from the National Airspace System of the United States.
developing an accurate capacity model that is applicable to the entire United States National Airspace System and that can be used in a wide variety of airspace design and management applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capacity model is validated by the peak count data.
the model is a useful tool for predicting capacity in a sector and for comparing the capacity potential of sectors.
this study validates that the model is a useful tool for capacity analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model captures the essential features of the capacity phenomenon in en route sectors.
the inherent capacity of sectors in the United States airspace is approximately 50 percent higher than the operational capacity.
the capacity model is validated for the US National Air Space System and that the inherent and achieved capacities differ significantly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the achieved capacity is significantly less than the inherent capacity, and that there is a large variation in the achieved capacity across centers.
the inherent capacity of the United States airspace is much greater than the achieved capacity.
the inherent capacity of the United States airspace is much greater than its achieved capacity.
